Use N–mm–MPa units throughout. The beam is a standard cantilever fixed at x = 0 and free at x = L, governed by Euler–Bernoulli beam theory (small deflection, linear elastic).
Given: L = 1800 mm, E = 200000 MPa, I = 1200000 mm⁴, P = 2000 N downward at the free end.
The bending moment varies linearly from P·L at the fixed end to zero at the free end.
Compute the slope at the free end using θ = P·L² / (2·E·I) and report the result in radians and in degrees.
Compute the vertical deflection at the free end using δ = P·L³ / (3·E·I) and report the result in mm.
Do not apply any additional boundary conditions or constraints at the free end beyond those inherent to a cantilever (zero moment, zero shear).
